overview.description: Dealer's Choice is a popular 'meta-format' for home poker games where the player in the dealer position chooses which specific poker variant will be played for that hand (or round). It emphasizes entertainment, variety, and the ability to adapt to shifting rules, ranging from standard Stud and Draw to eccentric wild-card 'invented' games.
overview.deck: 52-card standard deck (often two decks of different colors)

history.origins: Developed alongside modern Poker as a 'home game' tradition. While casino poker standardized games like Texas Hold'em for efficiency and house edge visibility, social clubs and home games leaned into 'Dealer's Choice' to level the playing field and keep the game fresh.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Variations of 'Dealer's Choice' appear in home game descriptions.
1970s: The WSOP introduces 'Mixed Games' which are structured professional versions of dealer's choice.
Present: A staple of casual card nights globally.
history.evolution: Has evolved from simple Draw/Stud choices to complex 'wild card' games (like Baseball or Follow the Queen) and even non-poker gambling games (like 7-27 or Acey Deucey).
history.cultural: Symbolic of 'Kitchen Table Poker' culture - informal, social, and prioritizing fun over strict professional GTO (Game Theory Optimal) play.

setup.players: 5-7 players (Ideal: 6). Too many players limit 'Shared Card' or 'Stud' variants; too few make 'Draw' variants less tactical.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Two packs of different colors are recommended (one being shuffled while the other is in play).
setup.equipment: Poker chips, dealer button, reference sheet for complex variants.
setup.dealing: The first dealer is chosen randomly. After each variant is complete, the deal passes clockwise.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best hand or inducing all other players to fold, based on the specific variant chosen by the current dealer.
rules.gameplay:
1. Rotation: Each player takes turns as the dealer.
2. Announcement: Before the deal, the dealer must clearly and concisely name and explain the variant (e.g., 'Seven Card Stud, high-low split, deuces wild').
3. Consistent Stakes: Betting limits and antes usually remain constant across the session regardless of the variant.
4. Dispute Resolution: The dealer's word is final on the interpretation of 'house rules' for that specific hand.
keyRules: The dealer must be able to explain the rules before starting.
Once significant betting action starts, the hand must be played out (no 'misdeal' re-calls for rule confusion).
Variants can include Draw, Stud, Shared-Card, Lowball, Hi-Lo, and Wild Card games.

strategy.basic: Call games you understand well and that punish the weaknesses of your specific opponents. If an opponent is overly tight, call a 'Wild Card' game to increase luck/variance.
strategy.intermediate: Position awareness: In a Dealer's Choice session, your strategy must shift drastically every 10 minutes. Be a specialist in knowing the transition between high-hand and high-low variants.
strategy.advanced: Meta-Game: Use your 'choice' to tilt opponents. Calling a complex or split-pot game right after an opponent loses a big pot can exploit their emotional state. Always keep a few 'eccentric' variants ready to break the rhythm of a player who plays too 'by the book'.
tips: Decide on your game before the button reaches you to keep the game moving.
Have a 'standard' backup game (like 7-Card Stud) if the group is tired or the hour is late.
Pay attention to the rules called! Missing a 'low-hole wild' rule is an expensive mistake.

list.name: Baseball

list.emptyOverridesReason: Baseball is a called variant; engine overrides would apply when this variant is selected.

list.name: Acey Deucey / In-Between

difficulty.easy: Calls 'Texas Hold'em' or 'Five Card Draw' every time. Plays strictly only high cards.
difficulty.medium: Maintains a rotation of 3-4 standard games. Adapts betting style to simple wild-card rules.
difficulty.hard: Selects variants specifically to counter-play the strongest remaining players. Models optimal betting for Hi-Lo split declarations.

considerations: Needs a library of 100+ sub-engines (Draw, Stud, etc) to swap between.
Must handle 'declaration' phases for Hi-Lo variants.
Requires logic for evaluating 'Option' fees (buying the middle card, etc).

ante.description: Pay the ante required to participate.
ante.constraints: Allowed only in phases that list this action as legal.

deal.reason: Deal procedure depends on the selected variant and is modeled via custom setup actions.

reveal_market.reason: Dealer's Choice has no default market reveal mechanic.

buy_market.reason: Cards are not purchased from market zones in core Dealer's Choice flow.

buy_stock.reason: This format does not use stock-buy actions as a default rule.

fold.reason: Fold behavior varies by selected variant and is not explicitly modeled here.

check.reason: Checking rules differ per called game and are abstracted in this baseline file.

call.reason: Call action specifics depend on the selected variant's betting structure.

bet.reason: Bet action details are variant-dependent in Dealer's Choice sessions.

raise.reason: Raise mechanics are controlled by whichever game the dealer has chosen.

declare.reason: Declaration is only used in certain called variants, not as a universal action.

reveal_hand.reason: Showdown reveal style changes by variant and is not fixed in this meta-format.

award_pot.reason: Pot-award logic depends on each chosen game's ranking and split rules.

play_card.reason: Some chosen variants use card play while others do not; no universal play action exists.

draw.reason: Draw behavior varies by selected variant and is not globally defined.

discard.reason: Discard rules are variant-specific in Dealer's Choice and not universal.

pass.reason: A general pass action is not consistently present across all chosen variants.

bid.reason: Contract bidding is only present in specific called games, not baseline Dealer's Choice.

meld.reason: Melding is not a default mechanic in this poker meta-format.

go_out.reason: Go-out win conditions belong to shedding/rummy styles, not this baseline poker framework.

customActions.description: Dealer chooses and announces the specific poker variant for the next hand.
customActions.constraints: Dealer-only at start of hand before ante and deal sequence.

customActions.description: Dealer states key variant rules, wild cards, and betting structure to all players.
customActions.constraints: Must occur immediately after variant selection and before ante posting.

engine.handRankingSystem: Hand ranking depends on called variant; default baseline is standard poker high-hand order.
engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

hero.title: DEALER'S CHOICE
hero.subtitle: Your Button, Your Rules
hero.tagline: The ultimate test of a poker player's versatility.

synthesis.shortDescription: The classic social poker format where the dealer calls the game. From high-stakes stud to wild-card whimsy, adapt your strategy to the rotating rules and keep your opponents guessing.

prompts.human: The button reaches you. The table is playing tight. Do you call a wild-card game to loosen them up, or stay with standard Stud?
prompts.ai: Game: Dealer's Choice. Format: Mixed. Current Dealer chooses variant. Strategy: Versatility and specialized rule knowledge.

scoring.description: Standard Poker hand rankings apply unless the chosen variant specifies otherwise (e.g., Lowball, Badugi ranking).
scoring.winCondition: Highest/Lowest hand or successfully bluffing the table.

nullReasons.targetScore: Dealer's Choice is typically session-based with independent hands rather than fixed target scoring.
nullReasons.cardValues: Poker uses hand rankings, not per-card point values; cardValues does not apply.
